career_ladder.note: Career progression for Civil Judges in the Tamil Nadu State Judicial Service is governed by the Tamil Nadu State Judicial Service (Cadre and Recruitment) Rules, 2007 (as amended) and the recommendations of the National Judicial Pay Commissions overseen by the Supreme Court of India. Senior judicial officers are eligible for elevation to the Madras High Court Bench under Article 217(2)(a) of the Constitution.

exam_scheme.note: Conducted jointly by TNPSC and the High Court of Madras in three successive stages: Preliminary screening examination (OMR, with 0.10 negative marking), Main Written descriptive examination (4 papers with mandatory sectional pass marks in each paper), and a compulsory Viva-Voce test requiring a minimum qualifying score of 18 marks out of 60.

stages.stage_name: Preliminary Examination (Objective Type - Single Paper, OMR Method)
stages.source_label: TNPSC Notification No. 12/2023, Section 'Scheme of Examinations: (A) Preliminary Examination'

papers.paper_name: Preliminary Law & General Aptitude Paper (Part A: Civil Laws & TN Rent Acts, Part B: Criminal Laws & Minor Acts, Part C: General Knowledge & Aptitude, 100 Qs)
papers.qualifying_threshold: 30 marks (SCs/STs) / 35 marks (BCs/MBCs) / 40 marks (Others); shortlist ratio 1:10 for Mains

stages.source_label: TNPSC Notification No. 12/2023, Section 'Scheme of Examinations: (B) Main Examination'

papers.paper_name: Paper I — Translation Paper (English to Tamil & Tamil to English of Pleadings, Depositions, Orders and Judgments)
Paper II — Law Paper I (CPC 1908, CrPC 1973, Evidence Act 1872, Principles of Pleading, Constitution of India)
Paper III — Law Paper II (Framing of Issues and Writing of Judgments in Civil Cases)
Paper IV — Law Paper III (Framing of Charges and Writing of Judgments in Criminal Cases)

stages.source_label: TNPSC Notification No. 12/2023, Section 'Scheme of Examinations: (C) Viva-Voce Test'

papers.paper_name: Oral Interview before High Court Judicial Board (Madras High Court, Chennai)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 18 marks (30%) out of 60 compulsory for all categories to be eligible for selection

financial_package.note: Salaries for Civil Judges in Tamil Nadu are determined by the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) recommendations implemented pursuant to Supreme Court orders in All India Judges Association vs Union of India. Entry-level Civil Judges (Junior Division) are placed on the J-1 scale (₹77,840 - ₹1,36,520).
financial_package.pay_source_label: TNPSC Notification No. 12/2023, Section 1: Vacancies and Pay Scale (Civil Judge cadre under Tamil Nadu State Judicial Service Rules / SNJPC Scale)
financial_package.estimate_note: Estimate assumes SNJPC J-1 entry basic pay ₹77,840 at 58% DA plus judicial allowances including Robe Allowance, Electricity/Water allowance, and official Judicial Quarters or HRA. Deductions include CPS/NPS, judicial welfare fund, and professional tax.
official_perks: Designated official judicial residence / bungalow with camp office facility
Official vehicle / conveyance allowance for court duties and inspections
Domestic assistance allowance / orderly support as per SNJPC allowances
Comprehensive medical facilities and reimbursement for officer and family
Robe allowance, sumptuary allowance, and judicial book/journal grant
Electricity and water concession as mandated by Supreme Court judicial directives

competition_benchmarks.note: Civil Judge examinations are held periodically based on vacancies certified by the High Court of Judicature at Madras under the Supreme Court Malik Mazhar Sultan guidelines.
